import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The retrieval side of compaction recovery is covered in
[session search + compaction recovery](/internal/docs/agent-insights/session-search-and-compaction-recovery).
This page is the **measurement** side: how to tell whether the recovery levers
(write-through discipline, the ~75% context-gauge nudge, `sessions:search`
self-recall, the compaction-aware `coord:orient { afterCompaction: true }`) are
actually reducing context loss — from data we **already** collect.

<Aside type="tip">
**No new plumbing.** Every MCP tool call is ledgered in
`harness_shared.tool_invocations` at dispatch time — `tool_name`,
`coord_owner_id` (the agent, migration 427), `args_json`, `invoked_at`,
`duration_ms`, `output_size`, `status`. So `sessions:*`, `coord:orient`,
`facts:assert`, `work_items:checkpoint`, and `loop:checkpoint` are all
countable today. Run these with `dev:pg_query` (read-only, `statement_timeout`
5s, row-capped) or the operator admin `psql`.
</Aside>

## 1. Write-through adoption — per-agent facts / checkpoint write rate

The core P-004 lever is behavioral: agents should flush a durable conclusion
**when it forms**. That shows up as `facts:assert` + `work_items:checkpoint` +
`loop:checkpoint` volume per agent. A live agent doing real work with a
near-zero write rate is the anti-pattern this measures.

```sql
SELECT coord_owner_id,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE tool_name = 'facts:assert')          AS facts,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE tool_name = 'work_items:checkpoint') AS wi_ckpt,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE tool_name = 'loop:checkpoint')       AS loop_ckpt,
       count(*)                                                    AS all_calls,
       round(
         (count(*) FILTER (WHERE tool_name IN
            ('facts:assert','work_items:checkpoint','loop:checkpoint')))::numeric
         / greatest(count(*),1) * 100, 1)                          AS flush_pct
FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations
WHERE invoked_at >= now() - interval '2 days'
  AND coord_owner_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY coord_owner_id
ORDER BY all_calls DESC
LIMIT 40;
```

`flush_pct` is a rough write-through-intensity gauge per agent. Trend it over
time (widen the window, `GROUP BY date_trunc('day', invoked_at)`) to confirm the
prompt-discipline note is moving the fleet, not just present.

## 2. Compaction-aware re-orient adoption

`coord:orient { afterCompaction: true }` is the structural rehydration lever
(re-delivers held-item checkpoints + armed-loop status + the self-recall
pointer). The `afterCompaction` flag lands in `args_json`, so adoption is a
one-liner:

```sql
SELECT count(*)                                                       AS orients,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE args_json ? 'afterCompaction')          AS after_compaction_orients,
       count(DISTINCT coord_owner_id)                                 AS agents
FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations
WHERE tool_name = 'coord:orient'
  AND invoked_at >= now() - interval '2 days';
```

<Aside type="caution">
As of 2026-07-05 this read ~1 `afterCompaction` orient out of ~950 — the flag
was new and adoption was near-zero.

**Update 2026-07-10:** adoption climbed sharply once the prompt guidance
propagated through a deploy — 521 of 903 `coord:orient` calls in the trailing
2 days carried `afterCompaction` (194 distinct agents), vs. the ~0.1% at
discovery. The lever went from "exists but unused" to majority-adopted in five
days; re-run periodically to confirm it holds as new agent cohorts spawn.
</Aside>

## 3. Self-recall usage — is `sessions:search` actually being reached for?

The retrieval lever only helps if agents call it. Count `sessions:search`
usage, and specifically the `session:'self'` (post-compaction self-recall) and
`mode:'verbatim'` (exact-quote) shapes:

```sql
SELECT tool_name,
       count(*)                                                    AS calls,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE args_json->>'session' = 'self')      AS self_recall,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE args_json->>'mode' = 'verbatim')     AS verbatim,
       count(DISTINCT coord_owner_id)                              AS agents
FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations
WHERE tool_name LIKE 'sessions:%'
  AND invoked_at >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY tool_name
ORDER BY calls DESC;
```

<Aside type="note">
At discovery (2026-07-05) `sessions:*` were new tools and expected zero rows
until exercised on the port telemetry aggregates (`:3070` serves green `main`,
not staging edits).

**Update 2026-07-10:** real usage now, over the trailing 7 days —
`sessions:search` 79 calls / 19 agents (38 `session:'self'`, 55
`mode:'verbatim'`), `sessions:read` 64 calls / 6 agents, `sessions:list` 5
calls / 2 agents. Non-zero, growing `self_recall` is the success signal —
agents retrieving instead of re-deriving.
</Aside>

## 4. The lossy-substring-grep tail should shrink

P-008 re-pointed `dev:claude_session op=search` and `omp:sessions op=search`
(raw substring greps) at the indexed `sessions:search`. Watch the deprecated
content-search path decline as the indexed path rises:

```sql
SELECT date_trunc('day', invoked_at)::date                          AS day,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE tool_name = 'omp:sessions'
                          AND args_json->>'op' = 'search')           AS omp_search,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE tool_name = 'dev:claude_session'
                          AND args_json->>'op' = 'search')           AS claude_search,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE tool_name = 'sessions:search')         AS indexed_search
FROM harness_shared.tool_invocations
WHERE invoked_at >= now() - interval '30 days'
  AND tool_name IN ('omp:sessions','dev:claude_session','sessions:search')
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```

<Aside type="note">
**Update 2026-07-10:** over the trailing 7 days, `omp:sessions op=search` and
`dev:claude_session op=search` both read 0, against 79 `sessions:search`
calls — the deprecated lossy-grep tail has fully drained onto the indexed
path.
</Aside>

## Caveats — what tool_invocations does NOT capture

- **Client-native tools are not MCP calls.** Claude Code's `Read`, `Grep`,
  `Bash` etc. are not dispatched through the operator, so "repeat reads of a
  file already read pre-compaction" is only visible for the MCP surfaces
  (`docs:get`, `plans:get`, `work_items:get`). For those, `docs:get` re-reads of
  the same slug post-compaction, and `metadata_json->>'truncated'` on the
  first read, are proxies — not a full picture of re-read waste.
- **Token cost is approximate.** There is no per-call token column;
  `output_size` (bytes of the tool result) and `duration_ms` are the closest
  ledgered proxies for re-orientation cost. A true token accounting would need
  new plumbing (out of scope for P-005).
- **`coord_owner_id` backfill.** The column (migration 427) is stamped
  going-forward; rows older than the migration have `NULL` owner. Keep windows
  recent, or filter `coord_owner_id IS NOT NULL`.

These are queries, not a dashboard — deliberately (P-005 is "document the
queries, no new plumbing"). If a standing scorecard is later wanted, register
these against the `scorecards:*` / rubric surface rather than adding a bespoke
report.
